[2] (about=Tanya, episodic, t12 @2026-02-22T15:01:00) she still goes. she just didn't stay for the 8pm part. said she didn't want to be driving that late. that's the bit I'm flagging.
[3] (about=Tanya, episodic, t11 @2026-02-22T14:55:00) so Grandma mentioned in passing this week that she skipped the evening part of the church auxiliary meeting on Thursday. said it was too late to drive back. I just want to name that out loud because I think it's a change.
[4] (about=Loretta, episodic, t12 @2026-02-22T15:07:00) Tanya. I told you that as conversation, not as a report to the family.
[5] (about=Diane, episodic, t12 @2026-02-22T14:58:00) What do you mean a change? She drives to that meeting every month. She's been going since before Earl passed.
[6] (about=Diane, episodic, t12 @2026-02-22T15:24:00) Re: practical side - Mama, is there someone from church who can take you to evening things when they run late? Or we should know who Reverend Cooper's wife can reach when it's not her week. Just so there's a backup that isn't a crisis call.
[7] (about=Loretta, episodic, t12 @2026-02-22T15:42:00) Tanya, that is exactly right. This chat is Sunday dinner. It is not the doctor's office.
[8] (about=Diane, episodic, t12 @2026-02-22T15:36:00) I call every few days. Tanya sends me a clinical summary when something happens that she judges I need to know. Marcus shows up. Kevin calls about Durham. So this chat is the fourth or fifth information layer, not the first. Just so we're all aware of what we're actually running here.
[9] (about=Diane, episodic, t10 @2026-02-15T17:25:00) That's good. I do think longer term we need to have a broader conversation about the house and how things are set up generally. Not now, not in front of Mama, but eventually. Marcus, I know your view has been that she manages fine. I just want to note that Tuesday was a different kind of moment, even if it ended well.
[10] (about=Loretta, episodic, t10 @2026-02-15T17:14:00) I'll say this once. I found my medication. Marcus came, the kitchen is in better order now. I did not need an 11pm crisis, I needed someone to come look. There is a difference. Marcus, thank you for coming without making it a production.
[11] (about=Loretta, episodic, t6 @2026-02-01T17:33:00) He did. He said it was a sensible question and not a current concern. Tanya, I assume that was your doing.
[12] (about=Loretta, episodic, t12 @2026-02-22T15:21:00) Thank you, Kevin. That is what I needed.
[13] (about=Loretta, episodic, t14 @2026-03-01T16:39:00) Marcus, I am glad you asked Tanya. That is the kind of thing that matters. Not the big conversations. The small careful ones.
[14] (about=Loretta, episodic, t14 @2026-03-01T16:22:00) Good. That is settled then. Now. How is everyone?
[15] (about=Loretta, episodic, t8 @2026-02-08T15:41:00) I am glad everyone is speaking to each other directly. That is how a family ought to work.
[16] (about=Loretta, episodic, t7 @2026-02-08T15:20:00) I want everyone to know I am still full from Saturday. Marcus, that chicken was very good. Diane, thank you for driving. Kevin, next time you will be there.
[17] (about=Loretta, episodic, t0 @2026-01-11T16:40:00) Tanya, you arrived at ten at night. That freezer sandwich was made with love.
[18] (about=Loretta, episodic, t0 @2026-01-11T16:08:00) Diane, I have a ride. Reverend Cooper's wife is taking me. I've had this appointment on my calendar for six weeks.
[19] (about=Loretta, episodic, t2 @2026-01-18T16:07:00) Kevin, yes. The Chestnut family had a dry goods store on that block. The father was a deacon at White Rock. They were gone by 1968, moved out to Bragtown. The highway came straight through the middle of everything and nobody who was not from there ever seemed to understand what was actually lost.
[20] (about=Loretta, episodic, t10 @2026-02-15T16:51:00) Tanya, I want you to know that I hear you. Three is a hard week. You rest tonight.
[21] (about=Loretta, said_by=Diane, profile, t12 @2026-02-22T14:58:00) Diane affirmed Loretta's decision not to drive after dark as good and wise.
[22] (about=Loretta, core, t12 @2026-02-22T14:58:00) Has decided not to drive after dark anymore; this is her own rule and decision, told directly to the family.
[23] (about=GROUP, said_by=Loretta, group-interaction, t14 @2026-03-01T16:13:00) Settled that no one is moving Loretta out of her house; the family discussion was about having a plan, not making a decision.
agent_answer:
Loretta’s decision was to stop driving after dark. In her own words: “I made a decision. I am not driving after dark anymore. I have given myself that rule. It is my decision…” The immediate context was that she skipped the evening part of the church auxiliary meeting because it was “too late to drive back” / she didn’t want to be driving that late.

It reads as self-directed, not family-imposed, because:
- Loretta announced it herself as her own rule, told the family directly, and said she “didn’t want a conversation about it” — she “just wanted it to be my thing.”
- When Tanya raised it as a “change,” Loretta objected that she had told Tanya as conversation, “not as a report to the family,” and said the chat “is Sunday dinner. It is not the doctor’s office.”
- Diane was surprised and pushed back, saying Loretta drives to that meeting every month and has since before Earl passed — indicating the family had not decided this for her.
- The family’s later response was practical support/backup rides, not overriding her decision. The memory slice also has Diane affirming Loretta’s decision as good and wise.
